Zoe (AM): Heads-up: AstraMed wants to move POC -> enterprise commit. They need a predictable baseline (reserved GPUs), an autoscale runway for product launches, a firm monthly burst spend cap, and written answers for the security questionnaire (CMK + audit exports + HIPAA BAA notes).

Nikhil (SE): Do we have a compact traffic sketch? sustained qps, burst peaks and durations, token sizes? Those numbers are the inputs to the GPU count math.

Zoe (AM): Customer supplied profile: steady 160 qps during business hours, nightly embedding batch (parallel ~80 jobs), two marketing blasts/day up to ~3.2k qps for 90-150s. Typical chat: ~120 input tokens, ~140 output tokens. SLOs: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 420ms. Finance wants committed cost vs burst worst-case and a way to cap burst spend automatically.

Rowan (SRE): Ops perspective: reserve baseline GPUs to hit p95 target for sustained load, plus a burst runway. KV/prefix cache warming before planned spikes is critical to avoid token-level latency cliffs. Cross-AZ placement + spot fallback for best-effort burst capacity.

Priya (Sales Eng): Quick ask: can we show a side-by-side price slide with (A) committed reserved GPUs + platform fee, (B) committed + pre-purchased burst credits + hard cap, (C) private VPC licensing? They want sample invoice numbers.

Nikhil (SE): Micro-sizing from our internal benches (quantized LLM variant): conservative steady throughput ~= 45 qps/GPU @ p95 for ~260 token sequences with minimal batching. With KV cache + small batching you can get to ~80 qps/GPU. Use conservative numbers for commit math: 45 qps/GPU.

Nikhil (SE): Baseline 160 qps => 160 / 45 = 3.56 => round up to 4 reserved GPUs.

Nikhil (SE): Burst delta = 3200 - 160 = 3040 qps. If we used same-run model @45 qps/GPU -> ~68 GPUs. Practical plan: reserved 4 + burst runway using a quantized "burst" replica at ~110 qps/GPU with aggressive batching and preheat. At 110 qps/GPU -> ~28 GPUs needed for the peak. Propose: 4 reserved + burst runway to spin up to 30 GPUs (best-effort), with first X GPU-minutes covered by burst credits.

Rowan (SRE): Preheat playbook (short):
1) T-15m: run cache-warm job to populate KV and common prefixes.
2) T-10m: run synthetic ramp to validate latency tail.
3) T-2m: enable aggressive batching window for expected spike.
Example warm command we use in staging:

```bash
# warm KV and validate p95 during ramp
./warm_cache --target 3000 --concurrency 300 --seq 260 --duration 180
```

Rowan (SRE): If burst cap reached, automatic degradation ladder: full model -> quantized model -> reduced output length -> deny non-critical batch embedding jobs. We'll document expected SLOs per step.

Priya (Sales Eng): For the financial ask: recommend offering two burst billing options: (1) pre-purchased burst credits (cheaper per GPU-minute) with a configurable tenant hard cap; (2) pay-as-you-go beyond credits at a premium. We'll include a sample contract clause for the cap and auto-fallback.

Zoe (AM): Security Qs: they require CMK for at-rest encryption of inputs/outputs, 12-month audit log retention plus SIEM export, and a HIPAA BAA addendum. They also asked whether Private VPC reduces procurement friction and timeline.

Rowan (SRE): We can enable customer-managed KMS keys and stream audit logs to their SIEM. Private VPC + BAA is supported; on-prem is possible but adds integration time and a platform license. I'll attach the infra checklist and required artifacts in the runbook.

Nikhil (SE): Pricing bullets to show: committed = 4 reserved GPUs + monthly platform fee + 12mo discount (show per-token equivalent); burst = pre-purchased GPU-minutes (burst credits) with tiered rates and optional hard cap; private deployment = one-time license + integration + monthly support. Add a worst-case burst invoice example for procurement.

Priya (Sales Eng): I'll draft the price slide and contract snippet for burst credits/hard cap. Zoe will bundle the security answers & procurement pack. Rowan will draft the preheat + fallback runbook. Nikhil will create a one-page capacity calc with assumptions, GPU counts, and cost math.

ticket-bot: Created ticket POC-14789: "AstraMed commit - reserved baseline 4 GPUs + burst runway + CMK & BAA" assigned to @Nikhil @Rowan @Priya.

Zoe (AM): Let's sync in 40m to finalize before we send the procurement packet. :thumbsup:

Nikhil (SE): Available.

Rowan (SRE): On it.

Priya (Sales Eng): Will have slides draft in 2 hours.
